newsitem.title: NORWAY: FOCUS - Two Norway banks post interest income drops.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Two Norway banks post interest income drops.

text.p: Norway's Den norske Bank (DnB) and Fokus Bank, battling shrinking interest margins, both reported lower net interest income in nine-month results on Thursday.

But DnB, Norway's largest commercial bank, managed to post a 5.3-percent net profit rise to 2.20 billion crowns ($345 million) from a year ago thanks to cost cuts, writebacks and other income to beat market forecasts. DnB shares was up almost a percent to 21 crowns in early afternoon on the Oslo Bourse.

Fokus, the country's third largest commercial bank, did not fare as well, with nine-month net profits falling eight percent to 383 million crowns. The weaker result was attributed to narrowing interest margins. Fokus stock was down 0.5 percent at 37 crowns in early afternoon trade.

Despite higher lending volume, banks are suffering from lower net interest income, their core business. Analysts attribute the drop in lower net income to the competitive situation in Norway's over-banked financial market and a generally lower risk of new loans.
But Fokus said reduced operating expenses was partly offsetting losses from the tight interest margin.
"Both banks seem to benefit from cost-cutting measures," an Oslo-based financial analyst said. "It is perhaps the most important thing that they have -- the flexibility to cut costs."
Fokus' operating expenses were trimmed to 620 million crowns from 649 million in the previous nine-month period.
"This shows that the bank is able to meet the increased competition by improved effectiveness," a Fokus statement said.

The company's net interest income fell to 689 million crowns from 730 million. Total other operating income fell by three million crowns to 330 million because of reduced real estate exposure and lower contribution from associated companies.

DnB nine-month net interest income fell to 3.17 billion crowns from 3.19 billion in the corresponding 1995 period, but other operating income rose to 2.10 billion from 2.07 billion with help from increased lending to shipping customers and new products, it said.

"The growth in the Norwegian economy and increased lending to shipping customers have contributed to controlled growth in lending, which has boosted (gross) interest income in spite of substantial pressure on interest margins," DnB group managing director Finn Hvistendahl said in a statement.
Third-quarter DnB net profits were 689 million crowns, a rise of 264 million relative to the year-earlier period.

"Efforts devoted to developing new products and creating stable sources of non-interest income have produced good results," Hvistendahl said. "This includes the sale of Vital's insurance products through the bank's distribution network."
Wholly-owned subsidiary Vital Forsikring ASA recorded after-tax profits of 214 million crowns, up from 201 million. The insurance firm contributed 106 million to group profits.
DnB's return on equity was 22.1 percent and earnings per share at 3.44 crowns.

Hvistendahl said operations in general showed sound performance. The managing director said the volume of problem committments had been further reduced and cost levels had been brought down as scheduled.
Total operating expenses fell to 3.36 billion from 3.50 billion. The operating profit before losses rose to 1.99 billion from 1.73 billion.
DnB's results were also further sweetened by net reversals on loans, or writebacks, into the accounts of bad loans turned good following the economic upturn several years ago.
The writebacks continued to decline and stood at 303 million crowns, down from 374 million in the year-ago period. ($1=6.383 Norwegian Crown)
